I tumori mixoidi (liposarcoma mixoide, m:
Myxoid tumors (myxoid liposarcoma, myxofibrosarcoma, intramuscular myxoma) contain a lot of water: on T2 they are hyperintense almost like fluid and may look like cysts. The difference is made by contrast (enhancement of the solid component, often patchy or reticular) or by ultrasound with color Doppler (internal vascularity).
A deep "cyst", intramuscular or near the vessels, several centimeters in size, without a typical location (ganglion near a joint or tendon) should not be filed as benign.
Myxoid liposarcoma affects young adults (30-50 years), especially the thigh; macroscopic fat may be absent or present only as thin streaks. It tends to metastasize to unusual sites (retroperitoneum, other soft tissues, spine), so staging also recommends spine (or whole-body) MRI in addition to chest CT. It is very radiosensitive.
